data.long_meaning: The name Shayam is derived from the Sanskrit language and it is a compound of two words - 'Sha' meaning god and 'Yam' meaning control. Thus, the name Shayam can be interpreted as 'The one who controls the god'. The name Shayam carries the meaning “God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Shayam usually hope their child will grow to embody god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It is believed that those named Shayam are blessed with the power to control and harness the divine energies of the universe. They are considered to be spiritual leaders and guides, who can inspire and uplift those around them.

The name is believed to bring blessings of control over one's destiny, and is often given to children who are seen as having strong and determined personalities. Additionally, in some regional traditions, Shayam is also considered to be an aspect of Lord Shiva, and is therefore associated with the power and strength of the god.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Shayam can be seen as representing the human desire to be in control of one's own life, to have the power to navigate the challenges and uncertainties of the world. It can serve as a reminder to strive for self-mastery and inner strength, rather than being a victim of circumstances beyond one's control. The name also reflects the ultimate truth that even the god of death, Yam, is under the control of a higher power, Lord Shiva, emphasizing the interconnectedness and hierarchy of all beings in the universe.
